ASTROQUEST – The Space Academy: An Interactive Space Science Learning Game

ASTROQUEST is an interactive space-learning platform designed to make space science engaging, accessible, and enjoyable for children aged 12 and above. We developed a concept for a web and mobile-based educational game where learners explore the universe through exciting missions, challenges, and simulations.

The platform features Planet Explorer, Space Science Lab, Lunar Outpost Construction, and Emergency Missions. It introduces two learning modes—Explorer and Commander—with adaptive difficulty to support different learning levels. Players learn about planets, space science, astronaut life, and space exploration while managing essential resources such as life support, power, and radiation protection.

ASTROQUEST addresses the challenge of making space education more interactive and practical rather than relying only on traditional learning methods. It is important because it encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and interest in STEM subjects while inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details: ASTROQUEST -THE SPACE ACADEMY ASTROQUEST – The Space Academy is an interactive space science learning platform designed to make learning about space exciting, educational, and accessible for children aged 12 and above, as well as anyone interested in space exploration. How It Works: ASTROQUEST transforms space education into an engaging game-based learning experience. It offers two learning experiences: Explorer Mode and Commander Mode. In Explorer Mode, users can explore planets, discover interesting space facts, and learn about the solar system through Planet Explorer and Space Science Lab. In Commander Mode, users take on astronaut-inspired challenges, construct a lunar outpost, manage resources, and complete emergency missions. The platform includes a three-indicator resource management system: Life Support, Power, and Radiation Protection. Users must make decisions and solve problems while maintaining these essential resources. An adaptive difficulty system provides challenges suitable for different learning levels. Benefits and Intended Impact: ASTROQUEST encourages curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, decision-making, and problem-solving skills. It makes complex space science concepts easier to understand through interactive activities rather than relying entirely on traditional learning methods. Our aim is to inspire young learners to explore science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and develop an interest in future space exploration. Tools and Technologies: The project is planned as a responsive web and mobile platform, with a Progressive Web App (PWA) approach. The development technologies and tools include: [Insert the actual programming languages, frameworks, design tools, and software used by your team.] Creativity and Innovation: The uniqueness of ASTROQUEST lies in combining space science education, astronaut simulation, resource management, interactive missions, and adaptive learning in one platform. Instead of simply reading about space, learners experience astronaut-inspired situations and make decisions that influence their missions. Factors Considered: Our team considered the target audience's age, accessibility, ease of use, educational accuracy, engagement, different learning levels, and the importance of making space science understandable and enjoyable. We also considered how to create an experience that is educational, challenging, inclusive, and suitable for both beginners and advanced learners. Through ASTROQUEST, we aim to turn curiosity about space into an exciting journey of discovery and learning.
